subject.title: [Feature Request] ACP Session Skill Context Injection

question: Should ACP `sessions_spawn` support OpenClaw skill-context injection, and if so which selection modes, redaction/audit fields, and child observability guarantees are part of the supported contract?
rationale: The source gap is clear, but implementing it decides whether trusted OpenClaw skill content may be copied into external harness prompts and how that interacts with native Codex skill behavior.

options.title: Start explicit-only with audit
options.body: Add only explicit skill-id selection first, with redaction, prompt-size limits, source hashes, and observable child load/invocation metadata before considering auto/default modes.

options.title: Defer to prompt parity
options.body: Keep ACP skill injection blocked until https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/95058 settles the owning prompt layer and lifetime semantics.

options.title: Keep ACP isolated
options.body: Reject OpenClaw core skill injection for ACP and require native harness skills, MCP bridges, or plugin-specific mechanisms instead.

recommendation.title: Start explicit-only with audit
recommendation.body: Add only explicit skill-id selection first, with redaction, prompt-size limits, source hashes, and observable child load/invocation metadata before considering auto/default modes.

likelyOwner.reason: The ACP spawn/runtime feature history starts with osolmaz's central ACP thread-bound agents work.
